writeup: TIC 450616233 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 6.0439 days, detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The system shows a primary eclipse with a depth of 5.35 percent dimming, while no secondary eclipse was detected. The signal registers a detection significance of 69.6 in the BLS periodogram analysis, and pixel-level difference imaging confirms a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 13.0, though the centroid offset measures 3.6 arcseconds from the target location. This candidate does not appear in any of six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel object. The machine-learning screening score of 0.54 indicates moderate confidence that this represents a genuine target, and the light curve passed all automated data quality checks without flags.
